name: null-related-assets
description:
REGRESSION LOCK on two null-valued fields Cyberint really emits. An alert with no related assets carries "related_assets": null, and `for a in item.get("related_assets")` iterated None, aborting the script with 'NoneType value is not iterable'. An alert with an explicitly null severity hit the same class of defect one line earlier: item.get("severity", "low") returns None because the key is PRESENT -- a .get default only applies when the key is missing -- and .lower() on None aborted too. Either one lost every alert in the response, including the healthy ones.

Both are now tolerated: the null severity falls back to low, and the alert naming no domain simply contributes nothing. The two alerts that do name store.example.com must land on one asset.

Skips namespaced_ids: cyberint ids are the domain with dots replaced by dashes and carry no tenant scope, a separate defect reported with the happy scenario. Extended with two non-object elements Cyberint could emit tomorrow: a bare string inside related_assets (used to abort at a.get) and a bare string in the alerts array itself (no id to key on, tallied with the id-less alerts and logged once).
